cultural.vision_reason: This is a Hawaiian feather-covered olonā fiber mat/apron with geometric bands (lozenges, triangles) in red, yellow, and black, matching a documented type of Hawaiian featherwork textile described in the museum's registration record.

physical.title: mat (formerly recorded as); apron
physical.summary:
Description in bound book of registration slips of Hawaiian artefacts, written c.1900 by James Edge Partington:
Broad band formed of strips of olona fibre fastened together covered on the face with feathers of different colours and in bands of various devices. Along each end are attached short cords of neatly plaited fibre.
L. 22.5", W.14.5"
[Addition in different handwriting] The main arrangement is a division into 5 vertical bands the groundwork of which is severally red, yellow, black, red & yellow again. On these are lozenges triangles &c in varied arrangements, the colours being black, white, red, yellow & green.
